1.title: DNS, Ingress and Gateway API
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: D N S, Ingress and Gateway A P I. It covers the exam area Services and Networking. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Understand and use Core D N S. Know how to use Ingress controllers and Ingress resources. Use the Gateway A P I to manage Ingress traffic. Practice with eleven hands-on labs worth seventy-eight points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Services and Networking (twenty percent). Practice in this module: eleven labs, seventy-eight points, about eighty-one minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: CoreDNS
1.text: Core D N S. Core D N S is the cluster D N S server. It runs as a Deployment (two replicas) in kube system, behind the Service kube dns whose Cluster I P is the nameserver in every Pod's slash E T C slash resolv dot conf (Lab eight point one). Pods. kube control get pods dash n kube system dash l K eights app kube dns. Service. kube control get svc dash n kube system kube dns. Configuration. Config Map core D N S, key Corefile. The default Corefile is a list of plugins inside a server block. fifty-three... Exam tip: After you edit the core D N S Config Map, restart the Core D N S Deployment so the change applies.

1.title: CoreDNS, continued
1.text: Core D N S. Kubernetes cluster dot local in addr dot arpa ip six dot arpa. answers Service and Pod names of the cluster. forward. slash E T C slash resolv dot conf. sends everything else to the upstream resolver (Lab eight point two). cache thirty. caches answers. errors, health, ready, prometheus, loop, reload, loadbalance. logging, probes, metrics, safety, auto-reload. hosts... extra static name to I P entries (you add this; Lab eight point three). Change the configuration (Lab eight point three): edit the Config Map, then restart Core D N S so the new Corefile is loaded at once.

1.title: Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster
1.text: Ingress: H T T P routing into the cluster. An Ingress is a set of H T T P(S) routing rules (host and path to a Service). It does nothing alone: an Ingress controller (a Deployment running a reverse proxy such as N G I N X or Traefik) watches Ingress objects and configures itself. Check what is installed. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: An Ingress does nothing without a controller: set ingress Class Name, and keep the backend Service in the same namespace.

1.title: Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster, continued
1.text: Ingress: H T T P routing into the cluster. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster, continued
1.text: Ingress: H T T P routing into the cluster. Imperative: kube control create ingress routes the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to a dot example dot com or a eighty the rule flag set to b dot example dot com or b eighty dash n ing one (a trailing or makes a Prefix path). Generate and edit with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml.

1.title: Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster, continued
1.text: Ingress: H T T P routing into the cluster. ingress Class Name. picks the controller; a missing or wrong class means nobody serves the Ingress (Lab eight point seven). host. match the H T T P Host header; omit for any host. path plus path Type. Prefix matches slash a and slash a slash b; Exact matches only that path. backend dot service. a Service in the same namespace and its port (number or name). default Backend. where unmatched requests go. tls. terminate H T T P S with the Secret's certificate. Test without D N S by sending the Host header to the controller's Service.

1.title: Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster, continued
1.text: Ingress: H T T P routing into the cluster. Common faults: wrong ingress Class Name; backend Service name or port wrong (typically a four oh four or five hundred two); Service has no endpoints (Module thirteen); backend in another namespace (not allowed); missing T L S Secret.

1.title: Gateway API: the successor to Ingress
1.text: Gateway A P I: the successor to Ingress. The figure shows this: Ingress and Gateway A P I. Exam tip: Remember the chain: Gateway Class, then Gateway with a listener, then H T T P Route with parent Refs.

1.title: Gateway API: the successor to Ingress, continued
1.text: Gateway A P I: the successor to Ingress. The Gateway A P I splits the job into roles and is more expressive than Ingress. It is a set of C R Ds (Custom Resource Definitions) plus an implementation (a controller); it is allowed in the exam (documentation at gateway-api.sigs.K eights.io). Gateway Class. Owner: infrastructure provider. Job: names an implementation (like an Ingress Class). Gateway. Owner: cluster operator. Job: a listener: port, protocol, which routes may attach. H T T P Route. Owner: application developer. Job: rules: hostnames, matches (path, headers), backends (with weights), filters.

1.title: Gateway API: the successor to Ingress, continued
1.text: Gateway A P I: the successor to Ingress. Check: kube control get gatewayclass,gateway,httproute dash A; kube control describe gateway web gw and kube control describe httproute routes show conditions ( Accepted, Programmed, Resolved Refs ) that tell you why a route is not working. Typical faults: wrong gateway Class Name; listener port or protocol mismatch; parent Refs pointing at the wrong Gateway name or namespace; backend Refs to a missing Service or wrong port; a route in another namespace when allowed Routes says Same.

1.title: Gateway API: the successor to Ingress, continued
1.text: Gateway A P I: the successor to Ingress. In the lab cluster: Traefik's H T T P entry point listens on container port eight thousand (its Service forwards port eighty to it), so the Gateway listener uses port eight thousand; the Ingress Class traefik is marked as the default class and the Gateway Class traefik shows A C C E P T E D True. Another implementation may use different ports and class names: always read kube control get gatewayclass,ingressclass and the controller's documentation first. Ingress versus Gateway A P I in one line: Ingress equals one object, H T T P only, behavior via controller annotations; Gateway A P I equals role-separated objects, richer matching and traffic splitting, portable.

1.title: Lab 8.1: dns server ip
1.text: Lab eight point one: dns server ip. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Pods in the cluster send their D N S queries to the cluster D N S Service. Find the I P address that a Pod uses as its nameserver (the nameserver line in slash E T C slash resolv dot conf inside a Pod) and write only that I P to about slash answers slash dns ip dot txt on the host. Confirm that it is the Cluster I P of the D N S Service. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 8.1: dns server ip, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get svc kube dns. Then kube control run dnsip the rm flag dash i the restart flag set to Never the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six dash q -- cat slash E T C slash, and so on. Then kube control dash n kube system get svc kube dns dash o json path dot spec dot cluster I P about slash answers slash dns ip dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 8.2: coredns upstream
2.text: Lab eight point two: core D N S upstream. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Core D N S forwards names that are not in the cluster to an upstream resolver. Read the Core D N S configuration (the Corefile in the Config Map core D N S in kube system ) and write the upstream that the forward. line points to (for example slash E T C slash resolv dot conf or an I P) to about slash answers slash upstream dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 8.2: coredns upstream, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get configmap core D N S dash o json path dot data dot Corefile grep dash n forward. Then kube control dash n kube system get configmap core D N S dash o json path dot data dot Corefile awk one forward print three about slash answers slash upstream dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 8.3: coredns custom host
2.text: Lab eight point three: core D N S custom host. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Make every Pod in the cluster resolve the name app dot corp dot local to the I P address ten dot one dot two dot three by changing the Core D N S configuration. Keep all existing settings. After the change, Core D N S must be running again (restart it so the new Corefile is loaded). Hint: the hosts plugin maps names to I P s. A new block goes before the forward line. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 8.3: coredns custom host, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get configmap core D N S dash o json path dot data dot Corefile slash tmp slash Corefile. Then sed dash i s ^ forward. hosts newline ten dot one dot two dot three app dot corp dot local newline fallthrough newline newline forward. slash tmp slash Corefile. Then kube control dash n kube system create configmap core D N S the from file flag set to Corefile slash tmp slash Corefile the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml then, and so on. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout restart deployment core D N S. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout status deployment core D N S the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control run lookup the rm flag dash i the restart flag set to Never the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six dash q -- N S lookup app dot corp, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 8.4: fix dns down
2.text: Lab eight point four: fix dns down. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Name resolution inside the cluster has stopped: Pods cannot resolve Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local. Find out why and fix it so that name resolution works again and Core D N S runs with its normal two replicas. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 8.4: fix dns down, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get deployment core D N S. Then kube control dash n kube system get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name kube dns. Then kube control dash n kube system scale deployment core D N S the replicas flag set to two. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout status deployment core D N S the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 8.5: ingress host routing
2.text: Lab eight point five: ingress host routing. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. An Ingress controller (Ingress Class traefik ) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing one, the Services a and b (port eighty) exist. Create an Ingress named routes that uses the class traefik and sends requests for the host a dot example dot com to the Service a and requests for the host b dot example dot com to the Service b, for all paths. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 8.5: ingress host routing, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get ingressclass. Then kube control dash n ing one create ingress routes the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to a dot example dot com or a eighty the rule flag set to b, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing one get ingress routes. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 8.6: ingress tls
2.text: Lab eight point six: ingress tls. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace ing two, the Service a exists. A certificate and key for secure dot example dot com are in about slash answers slash tls dot crt and about slash answers slash tls dot key. Create a T L S Secret named web tls from them, and an Ingress named secure (class traefik ) that serves the host secure dot example dot com from the Service a on port eighty and uses the Secret for H T T P S. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 8.6: ingress tls, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing two create secret tls web tls the cert flag set to H O M E slash answers slash tls dot crt the key flag set to H O M, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing two create ingress secure the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to secure dot example dot com or a eighty,tls web tls. Then kube control dash n ing two get ingress secure. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 8.7: fix ingress class
2.text: Lab eight point seven: fix ingress class. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace ing three, the Ingress site for the host site dot example dot com (backend Service a ) is not served: the controller answers four oh four. Find the cause and fix the Ingress (keep its name and rules) so that site dot example dot com returns the page of Service a. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 8.7: fix ingress class, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get ingressclass. Then kube control dash n ing three get ingress site dash o json path dot spec dot ingress Class Name echo. Then kube control dash n ing three patch ingress site the type flag set to merge dash p spec ingress Class Name traefik. Then sleep six. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 8.8: fix ingress backend
3.text: Lab eight point eight: fix ingress backend. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace ing four, requests for shop dot example dot com through the Ingress shop fail. The Service web is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Ingress so that shop dot example dot com returns the page of the Service web. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 8.8: fix ingress backend, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing four describe ingress shop then pipe to grep dash i -A two backend. Then kube control dash n ing four get svc. Then kube control dash n ing four patch ingress shop the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash rules slash zero slash http slash paths slash zero slash backend, and so on. Then sleep six. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 8.9: gateway httproute
3.text: Lab eight point nine: gateway httproute. This task is worth nine points, and you should plan about ten minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The Gateway A P I is installed with the Gateway Class traefik. In the namespace gw one, the Service a (port eighty) exists. Create a Gateway web gw with one H T T P listener named http on port eight thousand (class traefik, routes from the same namespace allowed), and an H T T P Route route a attached to it that sends the host a dot example dot com and all paths to the Service a on port eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 8.9: gateway httproute, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get gatewayclass. kube control dash n gw one apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 8.9: gateway httproute, Solution, continued
3.text: Lab eight point nine: gateway httproute, Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version gateway dot networking dot K eights dot io slash version one. Then kind H T T P Route. Then metadata name route a. Then spec. Then parent Refs name web gw. Then hostnames a dot example dot com. Then rules. Then - matches path type Path Prefix, value or. The remaining lines are on the screen.

3.title: Lab 8.10: fix httproute
3.text: Lab eight point one zero: fix httproute. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace gw two, the Gateway edge exists and the H T T P Route route should send a dot example dot com to the Service a, but requests are not served. Use kube control describe on the route to find the problem, and fix the H T T P Route (keep its name). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 8.10: fix httproute, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n gw two describe httproute route then pipe to grep dash i -A six Parents. Then kube control dash n gw two get gateway. Then kube control dash n gw two patch httproute route the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash parent Refs slash zero slash name, value edge. Then sleep eight. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 8.11: httproute weights
3.text: Lab eight point one one: httproute weights. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace gw three, the Gateway edge, and the Services stable and canary (both port eighty) exist. Create an H T T P Route named split attached to edge that handles the host app dot example dot com and sends ninety percent of the traffic to the Service stable and ten percent to the Service canary. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 8.11: httproute weights, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n gw three apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then sleep eight. Then kube control dash n gw three get httproute split. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Recall Check 1
3.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which Config Map holds the Core D N S configuration and which key? Answer: core D N S in kube system, key Corefile. Question two. Which plugin forwards non-cluster names to an upstream resolver? Answer: forward. Question three. After editing the Corefile, how do you make Core D N S load it right away? Answer: kube control dash n kube system rollout restart deployment core D N S.

3.title: Recall Check 2
3.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. An Ingress exists but nothing serves it. What do you check first? Answer: That ingress Class Name names an existing Ingress Class whose controller is running ( kube control get ingressclass ). Question five. Can an Ingress route to a Service in another namespace? Answer: No; the backend Service must be in the Ingress's namespace. Question six. What are the three main Gateway A P I objects? Answer: Gateway Class, Gateway and H T T P Route.

3.title: Recall Check 3
3.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. How do you see why an H T T P Route is not working? Answer: kube control describe httproute name: read the status conditions (Accepted, Resolved Refs). Question eight. How do you test an Ingress rule for a host without changing D N S? Answer: Send the request to the controller's Service with a Host header.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Here is the recap. Core D N S: Config Map core D N S ( Corefile ), Deployment in kube system, restart after editing. Plugins: Kubernetes, forward, hosts (extra names, needs fallthrough ), cache. Ingress: needs a controller; ingress Class Name, host, path plus path Type, backend Service in the same namespace. Imperative: kube control create ingress N A M E the class flag the rule flag set to host slash path svc port. Gateway A P I: Gateway Class - greater than Gateway (listener) - greater than H T T P Route (parent Refs, hostnames, rules, backend Refs). Debug: describe shows conditions; test with a Host header. In the next module, we continue the course.
